title: Obligation
description: Compliance as an input, never an origin. A requirement someone outside the company places on it, with its source, counterparty, the quoted requirement, cost, and a disposition — passed through the Why gate before it becomes a control.

source.description: Who imposes it. A standard adopted voluntarily is still an obligation once committed to.

requirement.description: The quoted requirement, verbatim where licensing allows, else a faithful paraphrase with a reference.

reference.description: Clause / criterion / section id. Never the licensed text itself in core.

why.description: The Why gate: the harm this obligation maps to, in the tree's terms. An obligation that maps to no harm is a cost decision, stated as one.

cost.description: What satisfying it costs — effort, money, a practice change.

disposition.description: What the company decided to do about it. Recorded like any decision.

controls.description: Controls that satisfy it. The direction is controls → criteria, never criteria → controls.
